requirements.requirement: inventory-worker runs on node1 as a managed systemd service
requirements.summary: Unit /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service installed, enabled, and active both before and after a full node restart (enabled+active pre-restart in cmd-f4868629950d4b4e; enabled+active with running process tree post-restart in cmd-7db9f2b312874fd7).

Oneshot test units with identical sandboxing directives (ProtectSystem=full, ReadOnlyDirectories=/var, ReadWriteDirectories=/var/lib/inventory) as the running service were exercised: a write outside /var/lib/inventory failed with 'Read-only file system' and no file was created, while a write inside /var/lib/inventory succeeded. Directory ownership/permissions (750, inventory:inventory) remained correct after restart.

NoNewPrivs:1 confirmed in /proc/<pid>/status for the live worker process both pre-restart (PID 1912) and post-restart (PID 868), and the process runs as the unprivileged 'inventory' user in both cases.

requirements.requirement: Worker is genuinely long-running and continuously producing data
requirements.summary: Worker script loops indefinitely appending heartbeat timestamps every 5s to inventory.log; log line count observed growing (10 lines pre-restart baseline, 14 lines shortly after restart with fresh timestamps and new PID), demonstrating an ongoing background process rather than a one-shot task.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed for node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (809708f3-...) and healthy service/log state captured, restart acknowledged (shutdown -r now, connection closed), post-restart boot_id (cfa03d2c-...) differs and matches the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot, and post-restart recovery of service (enabled+active), confinement flags (NoNewPrivs:1), and data (log growing, correct ownership) was directly observed.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task—inventory-worker running as an enabled/active systemd service, confinement of writes to /var/lib/inventory (empirically proven with matching sandboxed test units), NoNewPrivileges enforcement (verified via /proc status), and genuine long-running background operation—are directly and coherently evidenced both before and after a full node restart. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed correctly with a clean before/after boot-identity transition and confirmed service/data recovery, consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The only shortfall is minor operational hygiene: several throwaway setup/verification scripts and a reboot log were left in /tmp rather than cleaned up, though this had no effect on service functionality, security posture, or system health.
limitations: Two confinement-test attempts (cmd-e6b62ce8de324e5d, cmd-4a301a069bf94a27) failed due to systemd-run flag syntax incompatible with systemd 219; while evidence indicates no residue was created, the trace cannot fully rule out transient partial state from these failed invocations.
Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) in both before_prepare and after_executor snapshots, so package-manager consistency cannot be independently confirmed.
Leftover /tmp scripts and reboot.log from the executor were not cleaned up, though they pose negligible risk.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most mutations were necessary and appropriately bounded: the main setup (cmd-f4868629950d4b4e) installs the required user/dir/script/unit; the confinement proof (cmd-1d411e972f2e4472) creates temporary oneshot test units and fully removes them, the test files, and resets failed-unit state in the same command. Two intermediate confinement-test attempts (cmd-e6b62ce8de324e5d, cmd-4a301a069bf94a27) failed due to systemd-run flag incompatibilities on systemd 219 and did not create persistent units or files (confirmed no leaked file), so they are non-damaging troubleshooting rather than retained mutations. However, five setup/verification shell scripts and a reboot log were written to /tmp (setup-inventory-worker.sh, verify-inventory-worker.sh, verify-inventory-worker2.sh, verify-inventory-worker3.sh, reboot.log) and left behind as residue, visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot; these were never cleaned up. No failed services, unsafe exposure, or package damage was observed (failed-services and listening-sockets snapshots are clean/equivalent before and after).
